To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acyl-acylcarnitine is synthesized by a novel enzyme in E. coli that uses the same reaction mechanism as acyl-CoA thioester synthesis.
we have demonstrated a new enzyme, which we named acyl-acycl carrier protein synthetases (AAS) in E. coli, which catalyzes synthesis of acyl carrier protein (ACP) from long chain fatty acids and ACP.

we have identified and purified a soluble enzyme, acyl carrier protein synthetases, from E. coli that catalyzes the activation of fatty acids by acylation of the acyl carrier protein, and that the acyl-acylated acyl carrier protein can be used for the synthesis of membrane phospholipids in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of activation of long chain fatty acid for incorporation into phospholipids.
the elucidation of the mechanism of fatty acid activation in the biosynthesis of phospholipids.
the synthesis and utilization of acyl-ACP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

acyl-acycl-carrier protein synthetase catalyzes a reaction which is distinct from acylation by acyl-coenzyme A, that the enzyme is present in E. coli, and that the enzyme is involved in phospholipid synthesis.
the enzyme acyl-CoA:ACP transacylase catalyzes the reaction of fatty acyl CoA and ACP to produce fatty acyl-ACP.
acyl-acycl carrier protein synthetases are present in E. coli, that they have been purified, characterized, and that their role in the biosynthesis of phospholipids has been demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzyme catalyzes the following reaction: ATP + long chain fatty acid + acyl carrier protein (acyl carrier protein-SH) + H+ acyl carrier protein-S-acyl + AMP + PPi.
we have shown the existence of a new enzyme in E. coli, acyl-ACP synthetase, which catalyzes a reaction that is essential for the synthesis of phospholipid.
acyl-acylc arrier protein synthetase catalyzes the activation of long chain fatty acid with acyl carrier proteins and the reaction requires high concentrations both of Ca++ and Mg++.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fatty acid specificity of acyl-ACP synthetase is very broad, and that the enzyme is not specific for the incorporation of saturated or unsaturated fatty acids into phosphoglycerides.
the activation of long chain fatty acid by acyl-acylcarnitine synthase is an important process for the synthesis of acetyl-CoA.
the enzyme is a key component of the fatty acid synthesis pathway in E. coli and other organisms.
